title: Launchpad: compact inline assist strips & doc-anchor cards
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design compact, low-friction inline help strips ('Launchpad strips') that attach to core console surfaces and surface contextual doc links (doc-anchor cards). Strips should be visually minimal, keyboard-accessible, and support an expanded side tray for deep dives. Deliver assets for the March release with annotated screenshots and a small A/B test plan.
design_goals: Make first-time flows discoverable without interrupting experienced users
Provide one-click access to short docs, playground examples, and full PRDs
Ship accessible components (keyboard focus, screen-reader labels, color contrast)
Keep visual weight minimal so strips can be used in high-density pages (console lists, model catalog)
deliverables: Expanded side tray mocks with in-context screenshots and action buttons
Set of 8 annotated product screenshots for release notes and help center
Accessibility spec and keyboard interactions doc
Interaction prototype (Figma) and handoff package for frontend
acceptance_criteria: Collapsed strip shows short label, single icon, and accessible tooltip on hover/focus
Click expands either into small inline card (doc-anchor) or slides out side tray depending on route
Side tray includes header, 1–2 code snippets, 1 inline link to full docs, and a screenshot with masked account info
All variants pass color contrast >= 4.5:1 and keyboard focus order is logical
Design tokens and spacing defined for dev handoff; Figma components include variants and annotations
decisions: Use a single compact strip component reused across console surface instead of separate components per page (reduces engineering surface area)
Default behavior: collapsed strip opens an inline doc-anchor card; if card content > 240px height, prefer side tray to avoid layout shifts
Analytics hook: fire 'help_shown' and 'help_action' events with a 'variant' attribute for A/B testing
tradeoffs: Compact strip reduces discoverability for some users vs larger onboarding modals—mitigated by A/B test and ability to pin the strip
Embedding screenshots in side tray increases payload; we'll lazy-load and optionally serve lower-res for slow regions
Single component approach adds runtime complexity for routing logic but simplifies styling and accessibility maintenance
tasks: Design: final mocks for 3 surface types (model catalog, route config, deployment page)
Assets: generate 8 masked screenshots and export 2x, 3x sizes
Prototype: interactive Figma with keyboard tab flow and expanded tray animation
Handoff: annotated tokens and copy, create issue for ENG to implement variants
Testing: create accessibility checklist and run axe against a11y builds

accessibility_notes: Ensure strip is reachable via Tab and Shift+Tab; first action should be expand/collapse
Screen reader reads: 'Help: <short label>. Press Enter to open. Press Escape to close.'
When side tray opens, focus trap must be enabled; Escape returns focus to strip
All interactive elements include descriptive aria-labels and visible focus outlines
rollout_plan: Week 1: Dark launch to 10% of org accounts (feature flag) with analytics enabled
Week 2: Monitor CTR, pin rate, and time-on-tray. Run accessibility smoke tests across major browsers
Week 3: Ramp to 50% if no regression in error rates or negative feedback; otherwise iterate designs
Post-release: Add event-based alerts for sudden drops in help CTR and QA postmortem if issues arise
